Poppaea Sabina: Roman empress from 62 to 65 AD.

Founded in 1891 by Leandro N. Alem, this Argentine political party is the country's second-oldest active party and a longtime human-rights advocate that has been banned under military rule — which party?
Radical Civic Union: Political party in Argentina. The Radical Civic Union (Spanish: Unión Cívica Radical, UCR) is a major political party in Argentina.
Known by the abbreviation PRO and led by former Argentine president Mauricio Macri, which party has governed Buenos Aires since 2007?
Republican Proposal: Political party in Argentina.
This granddaughter of a Michigan governor chaired the Republican National Committee from 2017 until resigning in 2024, presiding over a string of election losses — who is she?
This Nazirite judge of ancient Israel slew a lion with his bare hands and later routed a Philistine army using only a donkey's jawbone — who was he?
Samson: Important character from the book of judges of the Hebrew Bible.
Born to a poor Cossack family and later a close ally of Stalin, this Soviet cavalry commander founded the Red Cavalry and became the subject of patriotic songs — who is he?
Only the second person to complete a full five-year term as Chief Minister of Karnataka, this Congress politician also served two stints as the state's Deputy Chief Minister — who is he?
Siddaramaiah: Chief Minister of Karnataka from 2013 to 2018 and 2023 to 2026.

On 26 September 1983, this Soviet duty officer judged his early-warning system's report of incoming U.S. missiles to be a false alarm — disobeying protocol and likely averting nuclear war. Who was he?
Stanislav Petrov: Soviet Air Defence Forces officer (1939–2017)

Running from 1912 to 1926 and named for its reigning emperor, this period in Japanese history saw political power shift from a group of elder statesmen to the country's parliamentary parties — what do historians call it?
Taishō era: Period of Japanese history from 1912 to 1926.
Serving as Lord Chancellor before becoming Archbishop of Canterbury, this cleric clashed with King Henry II and was murdered by the king's men in 1170 — who was he?
Thomas Becket: Archbishop of Canterbury from 1162 to 1170.
An economist who entered parliament via a 1981 by-election, this Samoan politician went on to serve as his country's prime minister from 1998 all the way to 2021 — who is he?
Tuilaʻepa Saʻilele Malielegaoi: Prime Minister of Samoa from 1998 to 2021. After Tofilau resigned in 1998, Tuilaʻepa became the prime minister and HRPP party leader.

Set to become just the fourth queen to rule her Scandinavian kingdom in her own right — and the first since 1720 — she is heir apparent thanks to a 1980 law that was Western Europe's first with absolute primogeniture. Who is she?
Victoria, Crown Princess of Sweden: Heir apparent to the Swedish throne (born 1977)
Erupting in 1793 as a peasant revolt that turned Royalist, this French Revolutionary-era conflict was fought south of the Loire river and gave its combatants the nickname "Vendeans" — what was it?
War in the Vendée: 1793–1796 set of battles between the French revolutionaries and the royalists.
First built in the 11th century after the Norman conquest, this Berkshire royal residence has been used by the monarch since Henry I, making it the longest-occupied palace in Europe — which is it?
Windsor Castle: Official country residence of British monarch.
Made by young Indonesians on 28 October 1928, this nationalist declaration proclaimed one motherland, one nation, and one unifying language — what is it called?
Youth Pledge: 1928 declaration by Indonesian nationalists.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Omar Khayyam (born 1048) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
C++ (founded 1983) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the oldest?
Haskell (founded 1990) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the astronomer from these four.
Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin is an astronomer. Despite completing her studies, because she was a woman Payne was not eligible to receive a degree from the University of Cambridge.
Who among these is a mathematician?
John Horton Conway is a mathematician. John Horton Conway (26 December 1937 – 11 April 2020) was an English mathematician.
What is the atomic number of Plutonium?
Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
What is the atomic number of Rhenium?
Rhenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Re and atomic number 75.
In what year was Jane Goodall born?
Jane Goodall: Dame Valerie Jane Morris Goodall ( GUUD-awl; née Morris-Goodall; 3 April 1934 – 1 October 2025) was an English primatologist and anthropologist.
In what year was Jan Hus born?
Jan Hus: Hus is considered to be the first Church reformer, even though some designate the theorist John Wycliffe.
In what year was Enrico Fermi born?
Enrico Fermi: With his colleagues, Fermi filed several patents related to the use of nuclear power, all of which were taken over by the US government.
In what year did Galileo Galilei die?
Galileo Galilei: Galileo has been called the father of observational astronomy, modern-era classical physics, the scientific method, and modern science.
In what year did Paracelsus die?
Paracelsus also had a substantial influence as a prophet or diviner, his "Prognostications" being studied by Rosicrucians in the 17th century.
In what year was Tardigrade discovered?
Tardigrade: The earliest known fossil is from the Cambrian, some 500 million years ago.
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The MiG-17 was license-built in China as the Shenyang J-5 and Poland as the PZL-Mielec Lim-6.
NASA X-43: Boeing. The NASA X-43 was an experimental unmanned hypersonic aircraft with multiple planned scale variations meant to test various aspects of hypersonic flight.
Cannoli: Italy. Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
Who is credited with discovering Copernicium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Copernicium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.
Who is credited with discovering Pluto?
Pluto: Clyde Tombaugh. Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Who is credited with discovering Influenza A virus?
Influenza A virus: Christopher Andrewes. Influenza A virus, or IAV, is a pathogen with strains that cause seasonal flu in humans; it can also infect birds and some mammals.
First flown in 1987, this medium-lift helicopter began as a joint UK-Italian venture between Westland and Agusta, and several countries use the nickname 'Merlin' for it — which helicopter is it?
AgustaWestland AW101 is a medium-lift helicopter in military and civil use.
In 1978, a run-in with a particle accelerator's proton beam left this Russian physicist with an extraordinary survival story after it passed straight through his head — who is he?
Anatoli Bugorski (born 25 June 1942) is a Russian retired particle physicist.
This discipline studies past human activity by recovering and analyzing artifacts, architecture, and other material remains through surveying and excavation — name the field?
Archaeology is the study of human activity through the recovery and analysis of material culture.

These shelled marine crustaceans, cousins to crabs and lobsters, spend their adult lives cemented in place filtering food from the water — and folklore once claimed geese hatched fully formed from one variety. What are they?
Barnacle are arthropods of the subclass Cirripedia in the subphylum Crustacea.
Known scientifically as Simuliidae, this family of small biting insects includes more than 2,200 named species, all but a handful belonging to a single genus — what are they commonly called?
Black fly (sometimes called buffalo gnats, turkey gnats, or white socks) are flies in the family Simuliidae of the Culicomorpha infraorder.
Often called a 'chest cold,' this inflammation of the airways in the lungs typically follows an infection that spreads down from the nose or throat. What condition is it?
Bronchitis is inflammation of the bronchi (large and medium-sized airways) in the lungs that causes coughing.
Standardized worldwide in 1907 as exactly 200 milligrams, this unit of mass is used to weigh gemstones and pearls, and is divisible into 100 smaller 'points' — what unit is it?
Carat (mass) (ct) is a unit of mass equal to 200 mg (0.00705 oz; 0.00643 ozt), which is used for measuring gemstones and pearls.
This woody perennial herb with bright blue flowers is cultivated for salad greens and a root that's roasted and ground as a coffee substitute. What plant is it?
Chicory (Cichorium intybus) is a somewhat woody, perennial herbaceous plant of the family Asteraceae, usually with bright blue flowers, rarely white or pink.
More closely related to lungfish and land vertebrates than to ordinary ray-finned fish, this ancient lobe-finned fish survives today as a single genus with just two known species — which fish?
Coelacanth are an ancient group of lobe-finned fish (Sarcopterygii) in the class Actinistia.
This is the capacity to produce novel, valuable ideas or works — whether an invention, a scientific theory, a joke, or a piece of jewelry — through the exercise of imagination — what's the capacity?
Creativity is the ability to generate novel and valuable ideas or works through the exercise of imagination.

Distinguished from their one-leaved cousins by a pair of embryonic seed leaves, this classic angiosperm classification was shown by molecular science not to form a single evolutionary lineage — which plant group?
Dicotyledon (or, more rarely, dicotyls), are one of the two groups into which all the flowering plants (angiosperms) were formerly divided.
Born in German Pomerania and drawn by Franz Boas into documenting Native American languages, this anthropologist became a founding giant of American linguistics — who was he?

Edward Sapir (January 26, 1884 - February 4, 1939) was an American anthropologist-linguist, and one of the most important figures in the development of the discipline of linguistics in the United States.
This class of chemical compounds forms when the hydrogen of an acid's hydroxyl group is replaced by a carbon-based group, and includes the fatty-acid derivatives called glycerides. What is it?
Ester is a compound derived from an acid (either organic or inorganic) in which the hydrogen atom (H) of at least one acidic hydroxyl group (OH) of that acid is replaced by an organyl group (R).

With over 2,400 described species, these soft-bodied beetles produce light mainly at twilight, an ability that likely began as a larval warning signal before evolving into an adult mating display. Name this insect family?
Firefly are a family of elateroid beetles with more than 2,400 described species, many of which are light-emitting.
First studied scientifically by an Augustinian friar experimenting with pea plants in 19th-century Brno, this branch of biology examines heredity and trait inheritance — which field?
Genetics is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity in organisms.
The first of America's Teen Series fighters, this twin-tail jet with swing wings debuted at sea on the USS Enterprise in 1974. What is it?
Grumman F-14 Tomcat is an American carrier-capable supersonic, twin-engine, tandem two-seat, twin-tail, all-weather-capable variable-sweep wing fighter aircraft.
Nicknamed the giant crab spider or cane spider, this member of the huntsman spider family is native to the tropics but has spread into subtropical areas — what is it?
Heteropoda venatoria is a species of spider in the family Sparassidae, the huntsman spiders.

Ranging from mild headaches and poor balance to severe confusion and seizures, this low-blood-sodium condition can be triggered by causes as varied as vomiting, diuretics, or overhydration — what's it called?
Hyponatremia is a low concentration of sodium in the blood. It is generally defined as a sodium concentration of less than 135 mmol/L (135 mEq/L), with severe hyponatremia being below 120 mEq/L.
Part of the fig and mulberry family and thriving in tropical lowlands, this giant of the produce world can weigh as much as 55 kg and measures up to 90 cm long — what is it?
Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus) is a species of tree in the fig, mulberry, and breadfruit family (Moraceae).
This Mexican-American astronaut flew on STS-128, led a branch at Johnson Space Center, and — urged on by President Obama — ran for Congress in 2012; who is he?
José M. Hernández (born August 7, 1962) is a Mexican-American engineer and astronaut.
This inflammation of the voice box causes symptoms ranging from a hoarse voice to complete voice loss, usually clearing up within two weeks. Name the condition?
Laryngitis is inflammation of the larynx (voice box). The primary symptom is loss of some vocal function, ranging from hoarse voice to no voice at all.
Only about 35 atoms of this synthetic element (symbol Lv, number 116) had ever been made as of 2020 — named for a California national laboratory. Which element is it?
Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
Sometimes nicknamed 'sea cows,' these large, fully aquatic herbivorous marine mammals can grow up to 13 feet long and include Amazonian, West Indian, and West African species — what are they called?
Manatee (family Trichechidae, genus Trichechus) are large, fully aquatic, mostly herbivorous marine mammals sometimes known as sea cows.

This cluster of at least three conditions -- including high blood sugar, high triglycerides, and low 'good' cholesterol -- raises heart disease and diabetes risk in roughly a quarter of American adults. What is it called?

Metabolic syndrome is a clustering of at least three of the following five medical conditions: abdominal obesity, high blood pressure, high blood sugar, high serum triglycerides, and low serum high-density lipoprotein (HDL).
Also called Indian mulberry, this tropical fruit tree contains harmful anthraquinones, and its foul-smelling fruit is mostly eaten only as a famine food — which species is it?
Morinda citrifolia is a fruit-bearing tree in the coffee family, Rubiaceae.
First linked by a Michigan doctor to farm wives sickened by isolation, this Gilded Age diagnosis grouped together fatigue, headaches, and a depressed mood — what condition?
Neurasthenia (from Ancient Greek (neuron) 'nerve' and (asthens) 'weak') is a term that was first used as early as 1829 for a mechanical weakness of the nerves.
Yellowing, thickening, and a nail separating from its bed are telltale signs of this fungal infection, far more common in toenails than fingernails — what's the medical name?
Onychomycosis is a fungal infection of the nail. Onychomycosis, also known as tinea unguium, is a fungal infection of the nail.
Taking place over 24 hours at a large investment bank, this drama follows employees navigating the earliest hours of the 2008 financial crisis. What film is it?
Passerine is any bird of the order Passeriformes (from Latin passer 'sparrow' and formis '-shaped'), which includes more than half of all bird species.

Sitting at the intersection of textual criticism, literary criticism, history, and linguistics, this scholarly discipline studies language through oral and written historical sources — what is it called?
Philology (from Ancient Greek (philologa) 'love of word') is the study of language in oral and written historical sources.
This birth defect results in extra fingers or toes, occurs more often in the hands than the feet, and has been linked to more than three dozen genetic mutations — what is it?
Polydactyly (commonly known as sixth finger and extra finger) is a birth defect that results in extra fingers or toes.

This medical specialty diagnoses, treats, and prevents disorders of cognition, perception, mood, emotion, and behavior, typically beginning assessment with a case history and mental status exam — name the field?
Psychiatry is the medical specialty devoted to the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of deleterious mental conditions.

This condition, often triggered by crush injuries or extreme exercise, causes skeletal muscle to break down so rapidly that it can turn urine tea-colored and damage the kidneys — what condition is it?
Rhabdomyolysis (shortened as rhabdo) is a condition in which damaged skeletal muscle breaks down rapidly.
Contracted from contaminated food, this bacterial illness typically causes diarrhea, fever, and cramps within a day or two of exposure — what is it called?
Salmonellosis is a symptomatic infection caused by bacteria of the genus Salmonella.
Setting a world record for mental calculation at London's Imperial College in 1980, this self-taught Indian prodigy also wrote books on math, puzzles, and astrology — who is she?
Shakuntala Devi (4 November 1929 - 21 April 2013) was an Indian mental calculator, astrologer, and writer, popularly known as the "Human Computer".
Beginning with stem cells near the basement membrane and passing through two rounds of meiosis, this process turns germ cells into haploid sperm inside the seminiferous tubules — what is it called?
Spermatogenesis is the process by which haploid spermatozoa develop from germ cells in the seminiferous tubules of the testicle.

Practiced by professionals who determine property boundaries and construction points using total stations, GNSS receivers, and lidar sensors, which technical discipline combines geometry, trigonometry, and law?
Surveying is the technique, profession, art, and science of determining the terrestrial positions of points based on the distances and angles between them.

Proposed by Albert Einstein in special and general forms published in 1905 and 1915, this framework superseded 200-year-old Newtonian mechanics and explains gravitation's relation to the other forces of nature — name it?
Theory of relativity comprises two physics theories by Albert Einstein: special relativity and general relativity. Special relativity applies to all physical phenomena in the absence of gravity.

Picture a spider that never learned to spin: these extinct arachnids lacked silk-producing spinnerets and wore an abdomen split into three or five distinct plates. Which order, known from the Silurian to the Permian?
Trigonotarbida is a group of extinct arachnids whose fossil record extends from the late Silurian to the early Permian (Pridoli to Sakmarian).
This chronic autoimmune disorder strips patches of skin of their pigment, and in antiquity was often wrongly conflated with leprosy — what is it?
Vitiligo is a chronic autoimmune disorder that causes patches of skin to lose pigment or color; these vary in size and can appear anywhere on the body.

An Iranian-born American surgeon specializing in bariatric and vascular procedures, this reality TV doctor became known for helping morbidly obese patients lose weight on the long-running series My 600-lb Life — name this doctor?
Younan Nowzaradan (born October 11, 1944), also known as Dr.
A pseudoscientific but ancient component of traditional Chinese medicine, this practice involves inserting thin needles into the body, most often for pain relief — what is it called?
Coined in 1852 but now considered stigmatizing in clinical settings, this WHO-estimated 283-million-person global condition involves continued drinking despite the harm it causes — what is it called?
Over 500 of these organic compounds exist in nature, yet only 22 appear in the genetic code, joining together to build proteins — what are they?
Amino acid: Organic compounds containing amine and carboxylic groups.

Serving as Surveyor of the Queen's Pictures while secretly working as the 'fourth man' of a notorious spy ring, this British art historian wrote a landmark 1967 study of the painter Nicolas Poussin — who is he?
Anthony Blunt: British art historian and Soviet spy (1907–1983)
Ranging from a racing tachycardia to a sluggish bradycardia, this catch-all term covers any heartbeat that strays from normal sinus rhythm — what is it called?
Arrhythmia: Group of medical conditions characterized by irregular heartbeat.
This Mexican mole salamander never grows up — it reaches sexual maturity while staying fully aquatic with feathery external gills, skipping metamorphosis entirely. What is it?
Axolotl: Species of salamander. The axolotl (from Classical Nahuatl: āxōlōtl [aːˈʃoːloːtɬ]; Ambystoma mexicanum) is a species of mole salamander.
A largely self-taught naturalist and astronomer born to a free mother in Maryland, he helped survey the District of Columbia and corresponded with Thomas Jefferson — who was he?
Benjamin Banneker: American scientist, surveyor and farmer (1731–1806)
Believed to descend from hounds once kept at a Belgian abbey, this scent hound can follow a human trail days old and is a favorite of police tracking escaped prisoners — which breed is it?
Bloodhound: Dog breed used for tracking by scent.
Grown on one of the Amazon's largest and longest-lived trees, this selenium-rich edible seed comes in a shell weighing up to 2 kilograms combined with its fruit. What is it?
Brazil nut: Species of tree and its edible seeds.
Native to tropical Africa, this gourd-producing vine yields fruit that can be eaten young as a vegetable or dried and hollowed out into bowls, ladles, or even musical instruments — what is it?
Calabash: Species of bottle gourd plant.
Ranked the world's richest person by Forbes from 2010 to 2013, this Mexican tycoon built his fortune largely through telecommunications and remains Latin America's wealthiest individual — who is he?
Around 20 millimetres long with a shimmering structural-green shell and a coppery underside, this beetle is identified by its isosceles-triangle scutellum — which species?
Cetonia aurata: Species of beetle. The scutellum is the small V-shaped area between the wing cases; it may show several small, irregular, white lines and marks.
This human-feeding ectoparasite is one of the world's great "nuisance pests" — yet despite carrying dozens of pathogens, no study has shown it transmits any disease to us. What is it?
Cimex lectularius: Species of true bug.
This umbrella term covers mental processes like perception, attention, memory, and reasoning that let us acquire and apply knowledge — what is it called?
Cognition: Mental process dealing with knowledge.
Born in 1863, this Italian is remembered as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry — who was he?
This herpesvirus genus's human species can cause mononucleosis in adults but birth defects affecting the eyes, ears, liver, and spleen when passed to a fetus — which virus?
Cytomegalovirus: Genus of viruses. The 11 species in this genus include Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV, HHV-5), which is the species that infects humans.
Marked by up to 20 liters of dilute urine a day and intense thirst that drinking barely satisfies, this condition comes in four types tied to problems with the hormone vasopressin — what is it?
Diabetes insipidus: Condition characterized by large amounts of dilute urine and increased thirst.
Working alongside biochemist Katalin Karikó on nucleoside base modifications, this University of Pennsylvania immunologist shared the 2023 Nobel Prize for enabling COVID-19 mRNA vaccines — who is he?
Drew Weissman: American physician and immunologist (born 1959)
First described in 1821, this family of large herbivorous mammals features a snout modified into a trunk and includes extinct relatives such as mammoths — which taxonomic family?
Elephantidae: Family of mammals. The family was first described by John Edward Gray in 1821, and later assigned to taxonomic ranks within the order Proboscidea.

Arising in the food pipe that runs between the throat and the stomach, this disease's two main subtypes are a squamous-cell form common in the developing world and a glandular form more common in developed nations. What is it?
Esophageal cancer: Malignant neoplastic disease of the esophagus.
Carried out by the lungs, kidneys, and skin in vertebrates, this bodily process rids the body of metabolic byproducts like urea, carbon dioxide, and uric acid — what is it called?
Excretion: Elimination of metabolic waste products by an organism.
Spending 36 years at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory contributing to America's robotic space missions, which Iranian-American scientist later advised high-tech startups after retiring in 2016?
Traditionally pounded from cassava, plantains, and cocoyam, this West African staple gets a shoutout in Chinua Achebe's novel Things Fall Apart — what dish is it?
Fufu: Dough-like food in African cuisine.
Ranging from Baja California to Japan's coast, this cephalopod is the largest of its kind on Earth and a common aquarium favorite — which creature?
Giant Pacific octopus: Species of cephalopod. It can be found from the intertidal zone down to 2,000 m (6,600 ft), and is best-adapted to colder, oxygen- and nutrient-rich waters.
One of China's 'Four Great Domestic Fish,' this herbivorous freshwater species was later introduced to Europe and the US to control aquatic weeds — which fish?
Grass carp: Species of fish. This Asian carp is the only species of the genus Ctenopharyngodon.
The son of a famous physicist and his first wife, this Swiss-American engineer taught hydraulic engineering at Berkeley and became renowned for research on sediment transport — who is he?

Hans Albert Einstein: Swiss-American engineer and educator. Hans Albert Einstein (May 14, 1904 – July 26, 1973) was a Swiss-American engineer, the second child and first son of physicists Albert Einstein and Mileva Marić.

First synthesized in 1940 by chemist Roger Adams via hydrogenation of THC isomers, this psychoactive cannabis-derived compound is sold in vaporizers despite never being drug-approved — which compound?
Lightest and most abundant element in the universe, it makes up about 75% of all normal matter and fuels the stars — colorless, odorless, and highly combustible. What element is it?
Hydrogen: Chemical element with atomic number 1 (H)
This contagious bacterial skin infection — usually from Staph or Strep — most often shows up as yellowish crusts on the face, arms or legs. What's it called?
Appointed FBI director by Barack Obama in 2013, this former federal prosecutor was fired from the post in 2017 — who is he?
Nicknamed "Marvellous Merchiston," this 16th-century Scottish laird discovered logarithms and popularized the decimal point — who was this mathematical wizard?

He coauthored the classic 1973 textbook Gravitation, advised Carl Sagan on wormholes for the novel Contact, and shared the 2017 Nobel Prize for the LIGO detection of gravitational waves — which astrophysicist?
Kip Thorne: American physicist, writer, and Nobel Laureate (born 1940)
This genus of bacteria mainly infects amoebae but can cause a pneumonia-like illness in humans when it spreads via poorly maintained cooling towers — what genus is it?
Legionella: Pathogenic genus of Gram-negative bacteria.
Only about 35 atoms of this synthetic element (number 116) had ever been made as of 2020 — and it's named for the California national laboratory that helped discover it. Which element?
Livermorium: Chemical element with atomic number 116 (Lv)

Originally built at a Boston hospital to manage patient records, this programming language pairs directly with an integrated key-value database and now underpins Epic's electronic health records — which language?
MUMPS: Programming language. It was originally developed at Massachusetts General Hospital for managing patient medical records and hospital laboratory information systems.
The heaviest members of the squirrel family, these ground-dwelling herbivores live in groups through the summer before disappearing underground to hibernate all winter — what are they?
Marmot: Genus of mammals (large ground squirrels)
This WWII German monoplane fighter formed the backbone of the Luftwaffe alongside the Focke-Wulf Fw 190, though Allied aircrew nicknamed it after its designer — which aircraft?

Messerschmitt Bf 109: German WWII fighter aircraft family. The Messerschmitt Bf 109 is a monoplane fighter aircraft that was designed and initially produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Bayerische Flugzeugwerke (BFW).
Named for the Latin for 'thousand feet,' no species of this many-legged arthropod class was confirmed to have 1,000-plus legs until a 2020 discovery with over 1,300 — what are they?
Millipede: Class of arthropods. Its primary defence mechanism is to curl into a tight coil, thereby protecting its legs and other vital delicate areas on the body behind a hard exoskeleton.
Produced by glands throughout the body's linings — including the respiratory, digestive, and urogenital tracts — which slippery substance traps and destroys harmful bacteria and viruses?
Mucus: Secretion produced by mucous membranes.

The Navy paid his Purdue aeronautical-engineering tuition under the Holloway Plan, and he flew the Grumman F9F Panther off the USS Essex in the Korean War before his most famous flight of all — which Ohio-born aviator was he?
A subsonic flying wing with a crew of two to three, this nuclear-capable stealth aircraft was built to slip past sophisticated air defenses for the US Air Force — what is it?
Northrop B-2 Spirit: American heavy strategic bomber.

Sitting between tissue and a full body system in life's hierarchy, this general term describes a structural unit built from functional tissue (parenchyma) plus supportive tissue (stroma), as seen in the intestinal wall — what is such a unit called?
Organ (biology): Collection of tissues with similar functions.
This skin sensation includes the classic 'pins and needles' feeling when a limb falls asleep, and can also be triggered by hitting your funny bone — what is it called?
Paresthesia: Dermal sensation with no physical cause.
In mathematics, what term describes both an ordered arrangement of a set's members and the act of rearranging them, as seen in the six possible orderings of three distinct numbers?
Permutation: Mathematical version of an order change.

A counting argument in mathematics: if you have more items than containers, at least one container must hold more than one item. Famous example: three gloves, but only two hand categories — what's this principle?
Pigeonhole principle: If there are more items than boxes holding them, one box must contain at least two items.
Looking like a jellyfish but actually a floating colony of cooperating zooids, this venomous siphonophore is also nicknamed the bluebottle — what is it?
Portuguese man o' war: Species of marine cnidarian.
This holotropical bird family comprises a dozen Afrotropical species and some 167 Neotropical species, including the blue-and-yellow macaw and the grey parrot — which family is this?
Psittacidae: Family of birds. The family Psittacidae or holotropical parrots is one of three families of true parrots.
After his Jewish family fled Germany, this engineer at Sanders Associates dreamed up playing games on a TV screen and built a 'Brown Box' that became the first home video game console — who is he?
Ralph H. Baer: American inventor and engineer (1922–2014)
This English anatomist coined the word 'Dinosauria' — 'terrible reptile' — yet remained an outspoken critic of Darwin's theory of natural selection — who is it?
Richard Owen: English biologist and palaeontologist (1804–1892)
Also known as brewer's or baker's yeast, this single-celled fungus believed to have originated on grape skins is one of biology's most-studied model organisms — which species?
Saccharomyces cerevisiae: Species of yeast. The species has been instrumental in winemaking, baking, and brewing since ancient times.
Comprising seven species from the flatback to the leatherback, five of these ocean-dwelling reptiles are threatened with extinction — what are they?
Sea turtle: Reptiles of the superfamily Chelonioidea.
Highly water-soluble and non-hygroscopic, this colorless compound with formula AgNO3 is the least expensive salt of its kind — which compound?
Silver nitrate: Chemical compound. It is highly water soluble colorless solid that is a precursor to many other silver compounds.
Combining vowel and consonant sounds into words for acts like persuading or declaring, this use of the human voice can even happen without any listener at all — what is it?
Speech: Human vocal communication using spoken language.
A bitter, colorless alkaloid from the seeds of the nux-vomica tree, it kills birds and rodents by triggering muscular convulsions and asphyxia. Which poison is it?
Strychnine: Poisonous substance used as pesticide.
Named after a figure from Greek mythology, this blue-gray transition metal with atomic number 73 is prized for corrosion resistance and shows up in capacitors inside computers. What element is this?
Tantalum: Chemical element with atomic number 73 (Ta)
This body region between the hip and the knee contains a single bone — the femur — that forms a ball-and-socket joint above and a hinge joint below. What is it?
Thigh: Body part between pelvis and knee; upper leg.
Caused by the parasite Toxoplasma gondii and often spread through undercooked meat or infected cat feces, this disease is famously dangerous to catch during pregnancy — what is it?
Normally containing two arteries and one vein cushioned in Wharton's jelly, this conduit links a developing fetus to the placenta — what is it?
Umbilical cord: Conduit between embryo/fetus and the placenta.
This ability to detect light and turn it into an image of one's surroundings can occur via daytime or night vision — what is it called?
Visual perception: Ability to interpret the surrounding environment using light in the visible spectrum.
This English economist and physician first made his name surveying Irish land to parcel out to Cromwell's soldiers, and is best remembered for his theories of 'political arithmetic' — who is it?
